t: Notwithstanding any provisions of this or any other  Act, during the fiscal year ending September 30, 1996, and hereafter, any department, division, bureau, or office may use funds appropriated by this or any other Act to install telephone lines, and necessary equipment, and to pay monthly charges, in any private residence or private apartment of an employee who has been authorized to work at home in accordance with guidelines issued by the Office of Personnel Management: Provided, That the head of the department, division, bureau, or office certifies that adequate safeguards against private misuse exist, and that the service is necessary for direct support of the agency’s mission.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Office of Personnel Management guidelines amount to rulemaking, or that the word "private" in "private residence" signals outside parties. But the section only authorizes agencies to spend appropriated funds on telephone service for federal employees working at home, subject to certification by the agency head. Every actor (agencies, OPM, agency heads, employees) is inside the federal government, and the text requires no public comment, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue.
fable.s: an employee who has been authorized to work at home in accordance with guidelines issued by the Office of Personnel Management

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes federal agencies to use appropriated funds to provide telecommunications equipment to federal employees working from home. The interaction is strictly between the federal government (the agency) and its own employees. There is no consultation, coordination, or participation required from parties outside the federal government (such as the general public, states, or private companies) in the decision-making process. The mention of 'private residence' refers to the location of the employee, not an external participant in a government decision.
qwen_block.s: any department, division, bureau, or office may use funds appropriated by this or any other Act to install telephone lines, and necessary equipment, and to pay monthly charges, in any private residence or private apartment of an employee who has been authorized to work at home in accordance with guidelines issued by the Office of Personnel Management

opus.w: This section does not involve participation. It only lets agencies pay for telephone lines in the homes of federal employees who are authorized to work at home. One could misread the mention of "guidelines issued by the Office of Personnel Management" as rulemaking, or the head of the office's certification as a review process. But the OPM guidelines are referenced, not newly authorized, and the certification is made by a federal official, so it stays inside the government. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
opus.s: Provided, That the head of the department, division, bureau, or office certifies that adequate safeguards against private misuse exist, and that the service is necessary for direct support of the agency’s mission.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes federal agencies to use funds for telecommuting equipment for federal employees. The guidelines are issued by the Office of Personnel Management, a federal agency. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities (such as the general public, states, or private organizations) in the decision to install these lines. The interaction is strictly internal to the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: any department, division, bureau, or office may use funds appropriated by this or any other Act to install telephone lines, and necessary equipment, and to pay monthly charges, in any private residence or private apartment of an employee who has been authorized to work at home in accordance with guidelines issued by the Office of Personnel Management
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "guidelines issued by the Office of Personnel Management" imply a process where employees or the public participated in creating those guidelines. However, the text itself only authorizes the use of funds based on existing guidelines and internal certifications. It does not describe the creation of those guidelines or any interaction with outside parties. The actors involved are federal departments, the Office of Personnel Management (a federal agency), and federal employees. All are inside the federal government.
